articles.title: Global Market: Japan bond yields edge higher ahead of key central bank meetings
articles.desc: Japanese government bond yields edged higher as investors assessed the monetary-policy outlook ahead of meetings by the Bank of Japan and the US Federal Reserve. Markets expected both central banks to keep rates unchanged while monitoring signals about possible December rate increases, inflation and economic growth.

articles.title: Tonbo Imaging shares soar another 17% after a 64% listing pop. Buy, sell or hold the stock?

articles.title: $7.7 trillion AI bet: Can hyperscalers earn enough to justify the spending?
articles.desc: Six major hyperscalers are projected to spend $7.7 trillion on AI between 2026 and 2030, but generating adequate returns will be a challenge. UBS estimates they need $1 trillion in additional earnings before interest and taxes by 2031. The key questions are whether AI boosts productivity and companies can monetise those gains.

articles.title: Jio’s record India IPO falls short of record payday for bankers

articles.title: Oil, US Treasuries prop up Indian bonds
articles.desc: Indian government bonds increased in early trading as oil prices declined, following a previous rally. The Brent crude price slipped significantly after hitting a six-month high last week, which impacted the debt market. Foreign investors have sold a substantial amount of Indian government debt since August, contributing to a prolonged rise in benchmark yields. Concerns over inflation and the Reserve Bank of India's rate decisions are influencing market sentiments.

articles.title: Rupee falls 5 paise to 94.98 against US dollar in early trade
articles.desc: In early trading, the rupee was priced at 94.98 against the US dollar, slipping by 5 paise primarily due to high crude oil rates and ongoing geopolitical conflicts. Despite the dollar index facing a slight decline of 0.15 percent, India's forex reserves have seen a downturn, potentially affecting the currency's stability. However, the Reserve Bank of India's timely intervention might bolster the rupee at lower trading levels.

articles.title: Holcim lifts guidance again on strong demand
articles.desc: Holcim has increased its full-year guidance due to robust demand for sustainable building materials. The company reported a 17% jump in recurring Ebit in the third quarter, surpassing expectations. Increased customer demand and cost discipline contributed significantly to this profit increase. The firm aims to announce around 15 acquisitions by the end of this year. Holcim is focusing on alternative fuels to mitigate rising energy costs.

articles.title: AU Small Finance Bank shares tumble 10% after Q2 results, but Jefferies and Motilal see up to 37% upside
articles.desc: AU Small Finance Bank shares fell up to 10% despite a 53% year-on-year rise in Q2 net profit. Jefferies and Motilal Oswal retained Buy ratings, citing growth prospects, improving asset quality and lower credit costs.

articles.title: Shriram Finance shares crash 6% as Jefferies, Citi, and other brokerages slash target prices after Q2 results. Why do they still say ‘Buy’?
articles.desc: Shriram Finance shares fell sharply on Monday after Jefferies, Citi and Motilal Oswal cut their target prices following the NBFC’s Q2 results. Despite concerns over rising credit costs and rural stress, all three brokerages retained their ‘Buy’ ratings, citing strong net interest income, resilient margins and long-term growth potential.

articles.title: Paras Healthcare allotment likely today: Check GMP, key details and how to check status
articles.desc: Paras Healthcare IPO allotment is expected to be finalised today after the Rs 1,450-crore issue was subscribed 2.23 times. With the GMP indicating a potential listing gain of around 1%, investors can check their allotment status on the MUFG Intime, NSE and BSE websites. The hospital chain is scheduled to list on October 28, 2026, after reporting a return to profitability in FY26.

articles.title: Coforge slips 3% even as Jefferies, Nomura, others raise targets after Q2 earnings. Why are they bullish?
articles.desc: Coforge shares fell despite strong Q2 results and brokerages raising target prices. Net profit surged 56.5% year-on-year to Rs 588.1 crore, while revenue jumped 54% to Rs 6,170.8 crore. EBITDA rose 67% to Rs 1,269.7 crore, with margins expanding 168 basis points to 20.6%. The company raised its FY27 EBIT margin guidance to 16%, while its 12-month order book grew 45% to $2.38 billion.

articles.title: Global Market: China's yuan hits four-year high as dollar weakens ahead of policy meetings
articles.desc: The yuan of China has surged to a peak not seen in four years against the US dollar, driven by evolving market dynamics and currency evaluations. The People's Bank of China established this daily midpoint, marking its strongest position since early February. Experts predict that this upward trend in yuan value may persist, citing signs of dollar softness intertwined with local policy adjustments.
